title: The Man of Lawlessness
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The man of lawlessness is the figure of final rebellion described in Scripture who opposes God and exalts himself before being destroyed by Christ. This doctrine calls for discernment and humility, not speculation beyond Scripture.
summary: The man of lawlessness is the figure of final rebellion described in Scripture who opposes God and exalts himself before being destroyed by Christ. This doctrine calls for discernment and humility, not speculation beyond Scripture.
christFocus: Jesus Christ will destroy the man of lawlessness by the breath of His mouth and the appearing of His coming. No rebellion against God can stand before the glory of the risen Lord.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Paul warns of a coming rebellion and a man of lawlessness who opposes and exalts himself. Scripture presents this as serious opposition to God before Christ’s appearing.

The details require humility. Believers should not pretend to know more than Scripture reveals, nor should they ignore what Scripture clearly warns.

The man of lawlessness is connected with deception, rebellion, false signs, and refusal to love the truth. This calls the church to hold fast to the Gospel.

His end is certain. Christ will destroy him by the appearing of His coming. Lawlessness may rage, but it cannot overcome the Lord.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
This doctrine is often mishandled through speculation, charts, fear, or reckless identification of current figures. Scripture’s purpose is more sober: warn believers and keep them anchored in truth.

The certainty of Christ’s victory gives courage. Even final rebellion is temporary before the King who reigns forever.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read this doctrine with humility and Scripture-shaped discernment. Refuse obsession, fear, and careless claims. Love the truth, hold fast to Christ, and remember that the Lord will defeat every rebellion against God.
